clue.text: Combining two illegal drugs makes one crazy

parts.note: crack is a smokable form of cocaine
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A warning that mixing two banned substances will drive a person mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two illegal drugs' supplies both pieces, and 'Combining' just puts them side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, the word describes eccentric, mad or foolish ideas and people.

clue.text: Subjects of genuine document

parts.note: genuine means real
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a document

explanation.surface: A query about the topics of an authentic paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Fields or domains of study and interest are subjects in the broad sense.

clue.text: Appeared ordinary in small part

parts.note: appeared, as in turned up, means came
O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: An actor who looked unremarkable in a minor role.
explanation.walkthrough: O for ordinary recalls Britain's old O (Ordinary) level school exams.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief appearance by a well-known performer in a film or play is a small role.

clue.text: Classic venue for women entertained by country music queen

indicators.note: being entertained by someone puts the women inside the singer's name

parts.note: Dolly Parton is a queen of country music
a hen party is for women only, so hen can mean women

explanation.surface: A historic concert hall where women are treated to a show by a country star.
explanation.definitionFit: The temple on the Athenian Acropolis is a building of classical Greece, a place or venue.

clue.text: Pictorial representation accomplished with gold after time

indicators.note: after time means the time abbreviation comes before the other pieces

parts.note: accomplished means skilled, able
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A picture achieved with gilt once time has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after time' tells you the time abbreviation leads, though the clue mentions it last.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a picturesque scene, often figures posed still as if in a painting.

clue.text: Spot daughter with fruit

parts.note: an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: Catching sight of a girl holding some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' reads as a verb meaning see, but it is a verb meaning to mark with spots.
explanation.definitionFit: To mottle something is to mark it with patches or spots of colour.

clue.text: Germany long in depression

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)
to long for something is to itch for it, so long gives itch

explanation.surface: A country pining away in a low mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' is a verb, a craving, not a length.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench or channel dug in the ground is a hollow, a depression.

clue.text: Tiger and pard shot as sort of game

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or shattered, so the letters of the two cats are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Two big cats shot by hunters as quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: A pard is an old word for a leopard; 'shot' is the anagram signal, not a hunting word.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is hunted for sport and food, so it is game in the sense of hunted birds.

clue.text: Trio belt out words from opera

indicators.note: out means wrong or in disarray, so the letters of the two clue words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Three singers belting out the lines of an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belt out' looks like a single phrase for singing loudly; 'out' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The text of an opera, the sung words, is called its book or script.

clue.text: Drive home in brougham merrily

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the run of the words brougham merrily

explanation.surface: Travelling home cheerfully in a horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: A brougham is a type of horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive home a point is to stress it forcefully, to pound it in.

clue.text: Excited to get in live coverage after a dip

indicators.note: to get in means the excited word goes inside the word for live

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist
athrob is an adjective meaning throbbing with excitement

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to slip into a robe after a swim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excited' gives a rare adjective meaning throbbing; 'to get in' puts it inside the verb for live.
explanation.definitionFit: A towelling gown worn to cover oneself after bathing is cover worn following a swim.

clue.text: Suave type, one captivated by some hot dancing

indicators.note: being captivated by something puts the one inside it
dancing means the letters of some hot move about into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A charmer swept away by some steamy dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges SOMEHOT to SMOOTHE, and 'captivated by' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-talking, polished charmer is a slick, urbane person.

clue.text: Hard men trap insect

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers, men
a net is a trap

explanation.surface: Tough guys catching a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: OR stands for 'other ranks', soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: The large stinging wasp is a kind of insect.

clue.text: Imprison lawyer in gambling organisation that's state of the art

parts.note: bang up is British slang for locking someone in a cell

indicators.note: in puts the lawyer inside the betting body

parts.note: the tote is the betting organisation at racecourses
DA is a district attorney, an American lawyer

explanation.surface: Jailing an attorney inside a bookmaker's firm sounds very modern.
explanation.walkthrough: BANG UP is British slang for imprison; the tote is a British betting system.
explanation.definitionFit: Fully modern, the very latest, is what the cutting-edge phrase means.

clue.text: Traditional singer of considerable weight embracing girl briefly

indicators.note: embracing means the heavy load wraps round the girl

parts.note: ballast is heavy material carried to steady a ship
Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana

explanation.surface: A heavy folk singer hugging a girl for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer of ballads, the traditional narrative songs, is a folk performer.

clue.text: Left enthralled by lookalike monarch for brief moment

parts.note: a twin is a lookalike

indicators.note: enthralled by means held inside the monarch

parts.note: a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A deserter dazzled by a ruler's double, if only for an instant.
explanation.definitionFit: 'In the blink of an eye' or 'in a trice' expresses an instant, a very short time.

clue.text: Standard way to get round initially common manner of speaking

parts.note: par is a standard or norm

indicators.note: to get round means the road surrounds the first letter

parts.note: a lane is a way or road

indicators.note: initially means take only the first letter of common

explanation.surface: A usual method for dodging the everyday way of talking.
explanation.definitionFit: The way a group talks, its idiom or jargon, is its particular speech.

clue.text: French art links two fish — a point used in the main

definitions.text: a point used in the main

indicators.note: links means the French word joins the two fish by sitting between them

parts.note: the marlin is a large sea fish
the pike is a freshwater fish
es is French for 'art', as in thou art, tu es

explanation.surface: A French art shop selling two fish, a point for sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is the archaic verb (thou art), French 'es'. 'The main' is the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors use the pointed iron tool to part rope strands when splicing at sea.

clue.text: Strike sovereign or pound

parts.note: to strike is to smack
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the sovereign

explanation.surface: Hit a gold coin or beat it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' and 'pound' both look like coins; only 'pound' is the definition. ER is Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a pound sterling, a one-pound note or coin.

clue.text: Youngster with knowledge about one set of races

indicators.note: about means the knowledge word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: ken is knowledge, as in beyond one's ken
I is the Roman numeral for one
TT is the Tourist Trophy, the motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A young person knowledgeable about a series of races.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is a famous motorcycle race series on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: A young cat is a juvenile animal, a youngster.

clue.text: Visually tired by keeping king in play

indicators.note: keeping means the little word by holds the monarch inside it

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragedy, its title king

explanation.surface: Eyes worn out by keeping up with a king on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like a link word but supplies its own letters, B and Y, round LEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes that are dim, watery and blurred from fatigue are tired-looking.

clue.text: Desire indefinite time in history?

parts.note: a year is a span of time in history, such as 1066
N is the mathematician's symbol for an indefinite number

explanation.surface: Longing for an unknown era of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: To long or crave for something is to have a strong wish, as a verb.

clue.text: Chemical compound produced from aluminium and potassium mixed with other metals we hear

parts.note: Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium
K is the chemical symbol for potassium

indicators.note: we hear means a word is given by how it is pronounced

parts.note: a metal mixed with other metals is alloyed

explanation.surface: A compound made from two metals combined with others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns ALLOYED into ALOID, which shares its pronunciation.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrogen-based plant substances such as caffeine and morphine form a class of organic chemicals.

clue.text: Doctor upset Greek character with pass

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so both pieces read backwards together

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: A medic distressed by a Greek with a ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns MUCOL, the Greek letter then the pass, to read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in physician temporarily covering for another doctor.

clue.text: An ant kit adapted for use against armoured vehicles

indicators.note: adapted means changed to suit, so the letters of an ant kit are reshaped

explanation.surface: An insect's kit modified for battle with tanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Weapons designed to knock out tanks are described with this military adjective.

clue.text: Provoke to riot, perhaps, able to be seen when broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so the phrase is pronounced

parts.note: something able to be seen is in sight

explanation.surface: Stirring up a mob, visible on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in sight' (visible) is pronounced the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up or urge on, as people to a riot, is the usual phrase 'to riot'.

clue.text: Physicist showing unaccustomed weight

parts.note: being new to something means unaccustomed to it
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A scientist putting on unexpected pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Isaac Newton discovered gravity, the force behind weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Isaac Newton was the English scientist who set out the laws of motion and gravitation.

clue.text: Government books supplying lot of soldiers

parts.note: a regime is a government
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: Official publications provided to many troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A large army unit, a body of troops, is a sizeable group of servicemen.
